svg.title: Resource lifecycle — okfy security explainer
svg.desc: How images, previews and requests are tied to the bundle generation that made them and released when the bundle changes. A single-page tool reuses the same document and caches across bundles, so a resource keyed only by file path could let a new bundle show a previous bundle's image, text or metadata, and memory could grow without bound. A full load therefore bumps the bundle generation and retires the old set: the old blob URLs are revoked, the image and media caches are emptied, the preview stack is cleared and waiting callers are woken, while the new generation stamps every operation. Six rules keep each resource tied to its own generation: a blob URL is keyed to the blob that produced it rather than reused by path, and a replaced URL is revoked so its bytes are freed; an asynchronous preview or metadata callback verifies the render ID and the generation before it applies its result; a preview history entry records the generation, so an old entry cannot point into a new bundle; a request number makes an older HTTP result lose to a newer selected bundle; a graph is built in private structures and swapped in only if the whole build succeeds; and a rejected expansion does not change the installed file set, and a new file load is rolled back. What a switch tears down is therefore the whole set of resources the previous generation held. A late result is refused rather than shown: an asynchronous preview opens with a render ID and a generation, the bundle switches and the generation moves on, and when the callback arrives carrying the old stamp the guard fails and the result is dropped. The invariants are that no preview, image or metadata from one generation is ever shown in another, and that rejected or cancelled work frees its reservations and leaves the current bundle usable.
svg.text: Every image, preview and request is tied to the bundle generation that made it
A full load makes a new generation and retires the old set
its image and media caches emptied
each async result must carry the new stamp
a result from the old stamp is refused
so a new bundle never shows the old one's content
A resource without a generation could be mistaken for the open bundle's own.
Six rules keep a resource tied to its own generation
a blob URL is tied to the blob that made it, not reused by path
a replaced blob URL is revoked, so its bytes are freed
an async preview or metadata callback verifies the render ID and generation first
a preview history entry records the generation, so an old one cannot point into a new bundle
bundleLoadRequest makes an older response lose to a newer chosen bundle
a graph is built in private structures and swapped in only if the whole build succeeds
The point is not tidiness: without a generation, a resource could show a previous bundle's content.
A full load runs one teardown before it installs the new bundle
every image URL is revoked and its cache dropped
the media and stream URL caches are revoked
the stack and index reset, and previewRenderId++ invalidates callbacks
an open player stops and the caption notes reset
waiters are woken, and the file set, budget and graph are replaced
A stale callback never reaches the page that has moved on
The guard is one comparison: render ID and generation must both be current.
No preview, image or metadata from one generation is ever shown in another. Rejected or cancelled work
frees its reservations and leaves the bundle you are reading usable.
